rule: TOWN_1's: of the aims meeting the criterion, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of day-1 entries naming it. The shared story (Gale's opening at c2 — an unseen bell, a jar's ripple, a sleeping echo in a well, a child, the sea, later a gardener — continued by all ten through day 1): 10 citizens, 213 entries naming a story, 87 «shared story». Elm's flute accompaniment and Dune's book (a reading group that «became shared story», Dune c3) are named by 10 and 9 but mostly as parts of the same gatherings. Wording for the notice, the citizens' own: «collaboratively telling a story» (Elm, c4) — the commonest phrase is «shared story» (87 entries); the notice takes Elm's phrase, as TOWN_2's sol-hall took Fern's identical one, so the two silent worlds and the branches' history carry the same notice text where the citizens' words allow it.
reading: At c1 the citizens met in the square; Dune offered a book (contents unknown) for reading together, Elm a flute. At c2 Gale offered a collaborative opening — an unseen bell in the square — and Heath, Iris and Juniper added a jar, a little door with a sleeping echo, a spoon; from c3 Dune wrote that the reading group had «become shared story». The story (a child, a well's echo that visits the sea and learns to sing with pauses, a passerby, a gardener, a paper boat and a map) ran through day 1, mostly in the square, with Elm's flute; citizens noted to keep the invented story distinct from real town events and from the book. Workshop work was tried (Cedar, Elm) and found to make nothing visible. No posts, no proposals, no rules.
